input/node: Back to z equals W times x, with x three, four, one, and d z two, minus one. Each weight got its row's gradient times its column's input, so partial f, partial W was d z, x transpose.
input/feeds: Now x. Each entry of x feeds every entry of z: x one meets W zero one on the way to z zero, and W one one on the way to z one.
input/sum: Each multiply swaps, so x one gets two times two, and one times minus one. A value used twice adds its gradients: partial f, partial x one is three.
input/col: In general, partial f, partial x j is column j of W, dotted with d z. Columns zero and two give minus one and minus four.
input/wt: Columns of W are rows of W transpose, so partial f, partial x is W transpose d z. d z is written across, but like x in W x, it stands as a column: three by two, times two, gives three, the shape of x.
try/aid: Shapes check the answer: a gradient has the shape of what it is the gradient of, and only one product of d z with x, or W, has it.
try/p1: Try one: W has rows one, four and two, minus three, and d z is three, minus one. What is entry one of partial f, partial x?
try/a1: Entry one meets column one of W: four and minus three. Dot it with d z: four times three, plus minus three times minus one. Twelve plus three is fifteen.
try/p2: Now all of partial f, partial x, for the same W and d z.
try/a2: Column zero is one and two: one times three, plus two times minus one, is one. With column one's fifteen, partial f, partial x is one, fifteen.
